text:
maria: FYI, p99 jumped from ~180ms -> ~1.2s on hosted-prod (us-west) around 22:00 UTC. Not steady — a 7m window. Long prompts + a bunch of tool calls in the traces. Rolling log excerpt attached.
aj: saw a couple alerts. timeline?
maria: 22:00:00-22:07 window. Heatmap shows kernel switches spike, EWMA microbatch increased variance, KV cache miss rate up. Link: <perfdash/runs/1978601234>
samir: quick hypotheses: (1) EWMA batch adaptation overshot because a few outlier gen requests spiked sequence len, (2) KV prefix "stickiness" caused heavy evictions when tool-call continuations expanded KV, (3) kernel selector flipping (matmul path selection) + compile fallback adds tail cost
lee: adding: selector picks matA for seq > 512. A handful of long prompts moved many requests above that boundary — we saw compile+fallbacks add ~200-400ms on affected requests.
maria: sample trace snippet: ```json
{"seq_len":1024,"kernel_path":"matA->fallback","kv_miss_rate":0.32,"batch_after_ewma":12}
```
aj: can we repro with the perf harness? I can spin a longprompt-heavy loadgen. Samir, any flags you want?
samir: try: `./tools/run_load --scenario longprompt-heavy --ewma-window 8 --hedging 0.0` to reproduce baseline. Then `--hedging 0.1 --ewma-window 4` to test hedging + faster adaptation. Also add `--kv-prefetch=on` to stress KV behavior.
perf-bot: Canary job started: canary-hedge-4 at 1978601250 (10% traffic).
aj: canary update after 5m: p95 stable, p99 improved ~30% vs baseline. Still seeing 2 hard outliers from requests that spawn recursive tool calls (depth 4+) — those create huge continuation tokens and thrash KV.
lee: thinking: short-term we can move kernel threshold from 512 -> 768 to avoid flip for common long prompts. Medium-term we need smoother kernel selection (avoid hard boundary). Also add compile cache TTL and prewarm heuristics.
maria: agreed. We also need metrics in console: kernel_switch_count, microbatch_size, ewma_batch_value, kv_evictions_per_min, toolcall_depth_hist. Add those before wider rollout.
samir: I'll instrument lightweight event logs for tool-call loop detection and add a counter for recursive tool depth. Also will prototype a cheap circuit-breaker: if depth>3, cap output tokens + mark request as low-batch-priority.
aj: rolling canary config: EWMA window=4, hedging=0.1, kv_soft_ttl=30s, kernel_threshold=768 for canary group. 10% -> 50% after 30m if stable. Promotion criteria: p99 < 400ms and no >5% host-level kv_eviction_hotspots.
maria: @oncall please keep an eye on canary graphs. If you see coordinated kernel recompile spikes or >3 hosts reporting KV thrash, abort.
oncall: on it — watching alerts and tracing streams.
aj: quick experiment note: reducing kv_prefetch from cluster->local-only dropped kv_evictions on the two hot hosts and improved p99 on those nodes. Might be prefetch policy interacting badly with hedging.
lee: also consider marking tool-call spawned continuations as "non-batched" (stream them) so they don't grow microbatch size. Might reduce batching pressure and KV growth.
maria: TODOs: 1) short-term: hedging + ewma tune + kv_soft_ttl + canary rollout (aj) 2) add counters to console + flamegraphs for kernel switch events (lee) 3) toolcall loop detection + circuit-breaker + event logging (samir) 4) reproduce and attach perf harness script + sample traces to ticket (maria)
aj: update after 30m: canary p99 down to ~380ms overall. Two nodes still show KV thrash — I reduced kv_prefetch to local-only and that helped. Continuing monitor.
samir: implementing depth-based circuit-breaker in a branch; will open PR WIP.
lee: I'll draft kernel-selector smoothing RFC (avoid hard thresholds, use hysteresis + compile prewarm).
maria: I'll open eng-runtime ticket with reproducer, attached flamegraphs, console dashboards, and assign samir/lee/aj. Tagging @oncall and docs team for rollout notes. :thumbsup:
aj: thanks — will post metrics in #eng-runtime-canaries channel as we progress.
perf-bot: Canary metrics updated: p95=120ms, p99=380ms, kv_evictions_host_top2=1.8x baseline.
maria: summary: short-term hedging+ewma tweak reduces p99; root causes appear to be (A) hard kernel thresholds causing compile/fallback tail, (B) microbatch adaption overshooting on outliers, (C) tool-call recursion causing KV cache growth and eviction storms. Medium-term fixes: smoother kernel selector, smarter kv eviction prioritization (stable prefixes), and tool-call circuit-breaker.
lee: noted. I'll coordinate with infra for compile-cache prewarm.
aj: continuing monitoring. I'll update thread with final rollout status.
end
